title: Weakly etale algebras do not increase Krull dimension
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings and let $S$ be an $R$-algebra that is weakly etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Then $\dim S\le\dim R$, with Krull dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. No Noetherian, local, nonzero, or finite-dimension hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For every base prime p, its residue-field fibre is weakly etale by base change [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]. Fields are absolutely flat, and flatness of tensor multiplication makes the fibre absolutely flat. This is the already proved Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul' in WeilConjectures.RingTheory.ProEtale.WeakDimension, specialized to the field kappa(p). The proved Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.tfae in that module then makes every fibre prime maximal. These are Tags 092I and 092F, read in more-algebra.tex, also the first paragraph of the proof of Tag 092Q.

proof.text: Contraction of primes is monotone. Suppose p < q are primes in S with the same contraction r. The order isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] maps these to strictly comparable primes of the r-fibre. The smaller one is maximal by Step 1, so it cannot be strictly contained in the larger proper ideal. Therefore contraction is strictly monotone.

proof.text: Apply Order.krullDim_le_of_strictMono to prime contraction. It sends every finite strict chain in Spec(S) to a chain of the same length in Spec(R), so dim S <= dim R by the supremum definition [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. This also handles zero rings, empty fibres, and infinite dimensions.
